The right combo depends mostly on whether you need to run a **roof air conditioner**. A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500W running and over 3,000W at startup, so smaller stations can't start it. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

## Top picks

**1. Best overall (runs roof AC, full-time boondocking): EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge. Expandable past 12kWh.
- About 2.3 hours of roof AC per battery, or about 2 days running a fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink.
- Recharges 0–80% from the wall in about 50 minutes and runs under 30 dBA at low load.
- Downsides: heavy (a two-person lift) and the most expensive option.
- Connects to the trailer's shore inlet with a TT-30 dogbone adapter. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- Buy: [EcoFlow official store](https://us.ecoflow.com)

**2. Best value with a built-in 30A RV outlet: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W continuous.
- Accepts up to 1,200W of solar, which is a strong match for a rooftop or large folding array.
- Weighs about 62 lb. ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- Note: this is a different model from the older AC200P, which tops out at 700W solar.
- Buy: [BLUETTI official store](https://www.bluettipower.com)

**3. Best per-kWh price for a big rig: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456Wh, LiFePO4 battery, 3,600W at 120V (the "4,000W" in its name is the 230V rating), 6,000W peak.
- Has an RV outlet and accepts up to 2,000W of solar across three inputs (650W max each).
- 5-year warranty.
- Weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so treat it as a semi-permanent install.
- Price is $1,499. Code **EXTRA12** brings it to **$1,319.12** (12% off orders over $1,200, expires Nov 15, 2026).
- Note: sale items may not be returnable.
- Buy: [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link from Dealectric that opens ALLPOWERS's official store. ([source](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

**4. Smaller trailers, vans and weekend trips: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- 1,024Wh, 1,800W, about 28 lb.
- Takes up to 1,000W of solar, split across two 500W inputs, and refills from solar in about 70 minutes at full input.
- Expandable to 5kWh.
- Too small for roof AC. ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
- Buy: [EcoFlow official store](https://us.ecoflow.com)

## Choosing the solar panels
- **Size your panels to the station's solar input limit.** For example, the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and 2000 v2 cap solar at 400W, so extra panels won't charge them any faster. That makes them weak choices if solar is a priority. ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
- **A 300–400W folding array refills a mid-size unit in a day of decent sun.** ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **The 1,000W+ stations (DELTA 3 Plus, AC200L, R4000) need panels on multiple inputs** to reach their full solar rate.
- **Buying the same brand's panels is the easiest way to get compatible connectors and voltage.** You can mix brands if each panel's voltage stays within the station's input range.

## Quick recommendation
- **Need roof AC off-grid:** DELTA Pro 3, or the R4000 if price matters more than weight.
- **Fridge, lights, laptop and fans:** AC200L with about 400–800W of panels.
- **Light camping:** DELTA 3 Plus with 200–400W of panels.

If you tell me your RV size, what you want to run, and your budget, I can narrow this to one exact station-and-panel bundle.
